name: Pedahel
overview: Pedahel was a male leader from the tribe of Naphtali, entrusted with the significant responsibility of apportioning the Promised Land among the tribes of Israel. His leadership role is specifically noted in the book of Numbers, highlighting his importance in the division of territory. This role underscores his standing within the tribe and among the Israelites during this critical period.
namesAndTitles: The name Pedahel means 'G-d [El] ransoms,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning that emphasizes God's redeeming power. This proper name, recorded in Numbers 34:28, was not given directly by God but carries a significant spiritual connotation consistent with the faith of Israel.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Pedahel was the son of Ammihud, establishing a clear familial link that situates him within a lineage of tribal leadership. Beyond this father-son relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Pedahel's role as the leader of the tribe of Naphtali in the apportioning of the land signifies his trusted position in executing God's command to divide the Promised Land. This task was crucial for the fulfillment of God's promise to Israel, as it involved the fair and divinely guided distribution of inheritance among the tribes. His inclusion in the narrative highlights the organized and divinely sanctioned process of settling the Israelites in Canaan.
